def summarize(df):
    summarized_df = pd.DataFrame({"Count (Non-Null)": df.count(), "Number of Unique Values": df.nunique(), "Column Data Type": df.dtypes})
    summarized_df.index.name = "Column Name"
    return summarized_df

#CLEANING
#this code assigns a community/neighborhood name to each of the entries in the My_CHI dataset that aligns with the data from the city of Chicago/census boundaries.

# Create GeoDataFrame from My_CHI dataset
geometry = [Point(xy) for xy in zip(project_data['Longitude'], project_data['Latitude'])]
my_chi_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(project_data, geometry=geometry, crs="EPSG:4326")

# Load the Chicago neighborhoods shapefile
neighborhoods_path = './datasets/chicago_boundaries/geo_export_26bce2f2-c163-42a9-9329-9ca6e082c5e9.shp'
neighborhoods_gdf = gpd.read_file(neighborhoods_path)

# Ensure both datasets use the same CRS
neighborhoods_gdf = neighborhoods_gdf.to_crs(my_chi_gdf.crs)

# Perform spatial join
my_chi_with_neighborhoods = gpd.sjoin(my_chi_gdf, neighborhoods_gdf, how='left', predicate='within')
# This cell helps process the data and prepare it for future visualizations
# 1) Processes paid program data into proportion paid programs by geographic area
# 2) Reads and prepares GPD file and adds in income column

filtered_price_data = project_data[project_data['Program Price'] != 'Unknown']
# Create a new column to categorize paid programs
filtered_price_data['Paid Program'] = filtered_price_data['Program Price'].apply(
lambda x: 1 if x in ['$50 or Less', 'More Than $50'] else 0)
result = filtered_price_data.groupby('Geographic Cluster Name').agg(
Total_Programs=('Paid Program', 'count'),
Paid_Programs=('Paid Program','sum')).reset_index()
result['Proportion_Paid_Programs'] = result ['Paid_Programs'] / result ['Total_Programs']

result.sort_values(by='Proportion_Paid_Programs', ascending=False)
proportion_mapping = dict(zip(result['Geographic Cluster Name'], result['Proportion_Paid_Programs']))

chicago_paid_programs_proportion = chicago
chicago_paid_programs_proportion = gpd.GeoDataFrame(chicago_paid_programs_proportion, geometry='geometry', crs='EPSG:4326')
chicago_paid_programs_proportion['centroid'] = chicago_paid_programs_proportion['geometry'].centroid

chicago_paid_programs_proportion['Proportion_Paid_Programs'] = chicago_paid_programs_proportion['community'].map(proportion_mapping)


#Cleans Program Price data

#Prints geosaptial plot of proportion of programs providing transportation by geographic area along with the corresponding income for each neighborhood, side by side with barplot

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12,6))

### Plot 1: Geospatial plot


# Filter out na values for transport provided
filtered_trans_data = my_chi_with_neighborhoods[my_chi_with_neighborhoods['Transport Provided'].notna()]

# Categorize programs by transportation provided
filtered_trans_data['Is Transport Provided'] = filtered_trans_data['Transport Provided'].apply(
    lambda x: 1 if x else 0)

# Aggregate data by Geographic Cluster Name
trans_result = filtered_trans_data.groupby('Geographic Cluster Name').agg(
    Total_Programs=('Is Transport Provided', 'count'),
    Transport_Provided=('Is Transport Provided', 'sum')
).reset_index()

# Calculate proportion of programs providing transportation
trans_result['Proportion_Trans_Provided'] = trans_result['Transport_Provided'] / trans_result['Total_Programs']

# Create a proportion mapping dictionary
proportion_mapping_2 = dict(zip(trans_result['Geographic Cluster Name'], trans_result['Proportion_Trans_Provided']))

# Create a new GeoDataFrame for transportation overlay
chicago_trans_programs_proportion = chicago.copy()

# Map proportion data to the GeoDataFrame
chicago_trans_programs_proportion['Proportion_Trans_Provided'] = chicago_trans_programs_proportion['community'].map(proportion_mapping_2)

# Calculate centroid for transportation markers
chicago_trans_programs_proportion['centroid'] = chicago_trans_programs_proportion['geometry'].centroid
chicago_trans_programs_proportion.set_geometry('centroid', inplace=True)

# Plot the income data as the base layer
chicago.plot(
    column='Income in Neighborhood', 
    ax=axes[0], 
    legend=True, 
    legend_kwds={'label': 'Per Capita Income ($)', 'orientation': 'vertical'}
)

# Add markers for proportion of transportation provided
chicago_trans_programs_proportion.plot(
    ax=axes[0], 
    color='orange', 
    alpha=0.5, 
    marker='.', 
    markersize=chicago_trans_programs_proportion['Proportion_Trans_Provided'].fillna(0) * 10000
)

# Set labels and title
axes[0].set_xlabel('Longitude', fontsize=18)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Latitude', fontsize=18)
axes[0].set_title('Proportion of Programs Providing Transportation \nvs. Neighborhood Per Capita Income', fontsize=12);

3.2 Analysis 2

By Pedro Nieto Rocha

# read the shape file, read all the datasets
shp_file = chicago
shp_file.set_crs(epsg=4326, inplace=True)
shp_file['geometry_polygon'] = shp_file['geometry']

# exclude O'hare 
shp_file = shp_file.loc[~(shp_file['community']== "OHARE")]
crime = pd.read_csv("datasets/Crimes_-_2022.csv")
data = mychi_data
crime['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(crime['Date'])
crime['updated_on'] = pd.to_datetime(crime['Updated On'])
data['Start Date'] = pd.to_datetime(data['Start Date'])
data['End Date'] = pd.to_datetime(data['End Date'])
# select observations where latitude and longitude or Location are not missing
has_latlong = ~data[['Latitude', 'Longitude']].isna().all(axis=1)
has_location = ~data['Location'].isna()
location_data = data[has_latlong  | has_location]
# remove the kansas observation
location_data = location_data[location_data['State'] != 'KS']
# drop the crime missing values as rows
crime.dropna(axis='rows',how='any', inplace=True) 
location_data = location_data.copy()
location_data.drop(['Image', 'Program URL', 'Registration URL', 'Registration Open', 
                   'Contact Phone', 'Contact Email', 'Hidden Programs', 'Featured', 
                   'Meeting Type', 'Has Free Food', 'Transport Provided', 'Participants Paid', 'Contact Name', 'Program ID', 
                   'Online Address', 'State', 'Registration Deadline', 'Scholarship Available'], 
                   axis='columns', inplace=True)
# convert the latitude and longitude into geopandas point objects
geometry = [Point(xy) for xy in zip(location_data['Longitude'], location_data['Latitude'])]
gdf_points = gpd.GeoDataFrame(location_data, geometry=geometry)
# set coordinate reference system
gdf_points.set_crs(epsg=4326, inplace=True)
# do a spacial join to find the communities for each of the points
points_with_labels = gpd.sjoin(gdf_points, shp_file, how='left', predicate='within')
points_with_labels = points_with_labels.dropna(subset=['community'])
points_with_labels = points_with_labels.loc[~(points_with_labels['community'] == 'OHARE')]
# select the programs from 2022, as the crime data only goes back to 2022
grouped_sizes = points_with_labels[points_with_labels['Start Date'].dt.year == 2022].groupby('community').size()
grouped_sizes_sorted = grouped_sizes.sort_values(ascending=False)
community_counts = points_with_labels[points_with_labels['Start Date'].dt.year == 2022].groupby('community').size().reset_index(name='count')
    
# do another spacial join of the grouped communities so for each unique community
community_gdf = community_counts.merge(points_with_labels, how='left', on='community').drop_duplicates(subset='community')[['community', 'count', 'geometry_polygon']]
community_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(community_gdf, geometry='geometry_polygon')

# define plot size
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6,5))

community_gdf.plot(
    column='count',
    ax=ax,
    legend=True,
    legend_kwds={
        'label': 'Number of Activities',
        'orientation': 'vertical',
        # create ticks in order to view orders of magnitude
        'ticks': [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 10000], 
        # make the bar a little smaller
        'shrink': 0.6
    },
    missing_kwds={'color': 'lightgrey'},
    cmap='YlOrRd',
    # add the logarithmic scale so that orders of magnitude can be appreciated.
    norm=LogNorm()
)

# do the same for the crime lat and long
geometry = [Point(xy) for xy in zip(crime['Longitude'], crime['Latitude'])]
crime_gdf_points = gpd.GeoDataFrame(crime, geometry=geometry)
# set coordinate reference system again.
crime_gdf_points.set_crs(epsg=4326, inplace=True)

# define function for IQR outliers.
def get_outliers(df, value_column, name_column):
    Q1 = df[value_column].quantile(0.25)
    Q3 = df[value_column].quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1
    lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
    
    outliers = df[
        (df[value_column] < lower_bound) |
        (df[value_column] > upper_bound)
    ].sort_values(by=value_column, ascending=False)
    
    return outliers[[name_column, value_column]]

import scipy

# get the global mean
global_mean_corr = community_correlations.mean()

def fisher_z(r):
  return 0.5 * np.log((1 + r) / (1 - r))

def fisher_z_test(r1, r2, n1, n2):
  z1 = fisher_z(r1)
  z2 = fisher_z(r2)
  se = np.sqrt(1/(n1-3) + 1/(n2-3))
  z_stat = (z1 - z2) / se
  # calculate two-tailed p-value using normal distribution
  p_value = 2 * (1 - scipy.stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
  return p_value

# select specific districts for analysis
districts_to_test = [
    'JEFFERSON PARK', 'WEST ELSDON', 'OAKLAND',
    'LOOP', 'WASHINGTON HEIGHTS', 'AVALON PARK'
]

print(f"Global Mean Correlation: {global_mean_corr:.3f}\n")

results = []
for district in districts_to_test:
  district_data = merged_df[merged_df['community'] == district]
  district_corr = district_data['program_count'].corr(district_data['crime_count'])
  n_district = len(district_data)
  n_global = len(merged_df)
  # perform statistical test comparing district to global
  p_value = fisher_z_test(district_corr, global_mean_corr, n_district, n_global)
  significant = 1 if p_value < 0.05 else 0
  
  results.append({
      'District': district,
      'Correlation': f"{district_corr:.3f}",
      'p-value': f"{p_value:.3f}",
      'Significant?': significant
  })

# convert results to DataFrame
results_df = pd.DataFrame(results)
print("Hypothesis Test Results:")
display(results_df)

######---------------Cleaning the 'Age' Columns----------------#########

# Discarding rows with 'Min Age' > 25, as is recommended by the My CHI My Future slideshow
mychi_data = mychi_data[mychi_data['Min Age'] <= 25]


######---------------Cleaning the 'Category Name' Columns----------------#########

original_categories = mychi_data['Category Name']

# Merging certain categories, so we only have 10 categories as opposed to 24
def category_merging_MATH(name):

    '''
    Function: Combines categories, separating 'Math' from 'Math' from 'Science + Computers'
    Arguments: name (String) of a row in the 'Category Name' column
    Returns: Recategorized name
    '''

    if (name == 'Computers' or 
        name == 'Computers.' or 
        name == 'Digital Media.' or
        name == 'Building & Fixing Things' or
        name == 'Science' or
        name == 'Nature'):
        return 'Science + Computers'
    elif(name == 'Math' or
         name == 'Science & Math'):
        return 'Math'
    elif (name == 'Law' or 
        name == 'Teaching' or
        name == 'Customer/Human Service' or
        name == 'Healthcare' or
        name == 'Transportation' or
        name == 'Social Studies' or 
        name == 'Work + Career'):
        return 'Career Specific'
    elif(name == 'Music & Art.' or
         name == 'Performance.'):
        return 'Arts'
    elif (name == 'Reading & Writing.'):
        return 'ELA' # ELA stands for English Language Arts, encapsulating both reading and writing
    elif (name == 'Helping Your Community.'):
        return 'Community Service'
    else:
        return name

mychi_data['Category Name'] = mychi_data['Category Name'].apply(category_merging_MATH) # Applying the category merging function
mychi_data['Category Name'] = mychi_data['Category Name'].str.strip('.') # Removing the '.' from the end of the category names
mychi_data['Category Name'] = mychi_data['Category Name'].str.replace('&', '+') # Changing all apersands (&) to '+' in the category names column, for simplicity

# Further categorizing the STEM category
def category_merging_STEM(name):

    '''
    Function: Combines categories, congregating 'Math' and 'Science + Computers' as 'STEM' ; this function is meant to be applied after category_merging_MATH
    Arguments: name (String) of a row in the 'Category Name' column
    Returns: Recategorized name
    '''

    if (name == 'Science + Computers' or
        name == 'Math'):
        return 'STEM'
    else:
        return name

mychi_data['Category Name'] = mychi_data['Category Name'].apply(category_merging_STEM)

# Adding an additional column called 'Subcategory Name', which is the original category name (not grouped)
mychi_data['Subcategory Name'] = original_categories


# Dealing with the rows that have 'Academic Support' in the 'Category Name'column - 

# if the 'Program Name' contains terms like 'English' or 'ESL', the 'Category Name' will be changed to ELA (English Language Arts)
# if the 'Program Name' contains terms like 'Math' or 'Mathematics', the 'Category Name' will be changed to Math
def update_category_name(row):
    if row['Category Name'] == 'Academic Support':
        if any(term in row['Program Name'].lower() for term in ['english', 'esl']):
            return 'ELA'
        if any(term in row['Program Name'].lower() for term in ['math']):
            return 'STEM'
    else:
        return row['Category Name']
mychi_data['Category Name'] = mychi_data.apply(update_category_name, axis=1)


######---------------Creating new variables----------------#########

# Creating `age_group` column

def get_age_group(row):

    '''
    Function: Used with .apply() to determint the age groups for each row in the dataset
    Arguments: row (Series) of a DataFrame
    Returns: Age group
    '''
    
    min_age = row['Min Age']
    max_age = row['Max Age']

    if max_age > 25:
        return 'Family'
    elif max_age < 6:
        return 'Toddlers'
    elif max_age < 13:
        return 'Children'
    elif max_age < 19:
        return 'Teenagers'
    else:
        return 'Adults'

mychi_data['age_group'] = mychi_data.apply(get_age_group, axis=1)


######---------------Outlier Detection & Handling of Latitude and Longitude Columns----------------#########

# Removing programs that have Latitude or Longitude outside of the boundaries of Chicago

def mark_outliers(row):
    if (row['Latitude'] < 43 and row['Latitude'] > 41.5) and (row['Longitude'] < -87.4 and row['Longitude'] > -87.9):
        return 'Keep'
    else:
        return 'Remove'
    
mychi_data = mychi_data[mychi_data.apply(mark_outliers, axis=1) == 'Keep']

######---------------Extracting/Editing Needed Columns----------------#########

# This is a HUGE dataset that contains many different metrics. We want to only extract the Reading and Math `Attainment` scores for all grade levels
# Note: The attainment scores come from two different exam types for high-schoolers (PSAT and SAT) and non-high schoolers (NWEA), so we need to extract both
# We also only want to look at the percentages, not the percentiles, so we filter the data to drop the percentiles columns, which contain `_Lbl` at the end of their name, as opposed to `_Pct`
relevant_columns = [col for col in progress_reports_19.columns if 
                        ("Math" in col or "Reading" in col) and 
                        ("_Pct" in col) and 
                        ("Grade" in col) and
                        ("PSAT" in col or "SAT" in col or "Attainment" in col)]
scores19 = progress_reports_19[relevant_columns]



# Renaming columns for simplicity, removing extraneous characters in the column names
scores19 = scores19.rename(columns=lambda x: x.replace("_Pct", ""))
scores19 = scores19.rename(columns=lambda x: x.replace("NWEA_", ""))
scores19 = scores19.rename(columns=lambda x: x.replace("PSAT_", ""))
scores19 = scores19.rename(columns=lambda x: x.replace("SAT_", ""))
scores19 = scores19.rename(columns=lambda x: x.replace("_Attainment", ""))
scores19 = scores19.rename(columns=lambda x: x.replace("_Grade", ""))
scores19 = scores19.rename(columns=lambda x: x.replace("Growth_", ""))
scores19 = scores19.rename(columns=lambda x: x.replace("_School", ""))
scores19 = scores19.rename(columns=lambda x: x.replace("Reading", "ELA"))

# Dropping rows (schools) who have all NaN values (probably a result of schools choosing not to report their grades), and sorting by the column names
scores19.dropna(axis=0,how='all', inplace=True)
scores19.sort_index(axis=1, ascending=False, inplace=True)



######---------------Imputing Missing Values of Math/Reading Scores----------------#########

# I will impute the NaN values with the school's average attainment score for the given subject

# Creating a hierarchical index to easily group and impute the NaN values
new_columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples( 
    [(col.split('_')[0], col.split('_')[1]) for col in scores19.columns],
    names=['Subject', 'Level'])
scores19.columns = new_columns 

# Imputing values
reading_means = scores19['ELA'].mean(axis=1)
math_means = scores19['Math'].mean(axis=1)
scores19['ELA'] = scores19['ELA'].apply(lambda x: x.fillna(reading_means[x.name]), axis=1)
scores19['Math'] = scores19['Math'].apply(lambda x: x.fillna(math_means[x.name]), axis=1)
# Stacking the data to wide to long format
stacked_progress_reports_19 = (scores19
                       .stack(level=0, future_stack=True)
                       .stack(level=0, future_stack=True)
                       .reset_index()
                       .drop(columns=['level_0'])
                       .rename(columns={0: 'Score'})
)

from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap

# removing O'Hare from the GeoPandas dataframe
chicago = chicago[chicago['community'] != 'OHARE']

# Extracting the needed information (Latitude, Longitude, and Average Standardized Test Scores) from each row in the progress_reports_19 dataset

schools_mean_scores = scores19.apply(lambda x: x.mean(), axis=1)
correct_indices = schools_mean_scores.index
locations_correct_indices = progress_reports_19[['School_Latitude', 'School_Longitude']].loc[correct_indices]

location_and_scores = pd.concat([schools_mean_scores, locations_correct_indices], axis=1).rename(columns={0:'Mean Test Score', 'School_Latitude':'Latitude', 'School_Longitude':'Longitude'})

# Adding a column for the GeoPandas coordinate pair for simple plotting
geo = [Point(xy) for xy in zip(location_and_scores.Longitude, location_and_scores.Latitude)]
location_and_scores_geo = gpd.GeoDataFrame(location_and_scores, geometry=geo, crs='epsg:4326') # specifying the correct coordinate system

# Associating each school with a neighborhood --> results in a GeoPandas dataframe with a neighborhood column for each school
chicago = chicago.to_crs('epsg:4326') # specifying the correct coordinate system for the OTHER GeoPandas dataframe
neighborhoods_schools = gpd.sjoin(location_and_scores_geo, chicago, how='inner', predicate='within')

# Caclulating the Average Standardized Test Scores for each neighborhood --> results in a DF with rows corresponding to unique neighborhoods, with a column for the neighborhood's average test score
neighborhoods_avg_test_scores = neighborhoods_schools.groupby('community')['Mean Test Score'].mean().reset_index()

# Merging the average test scores with the neighborhoods dataframe --> results in a the chicago dataframe with a column for the neighborhood's average test score
chicago_test_scores = chicago.merge(neighborhoods_avg_test_scores, on='community', how='left')


### Creating the plots

fig, [(ax1, ax2), (ax3, ax4)] = plt.subplots(2,2, figsize=(8,6))


def extract_plottable_info(data, age_level, subject):

    '''
    Function: Uses Geopandas to extract information from the progress reports data and prepare it to be geo-plotted
    Arguments: Unprepared data, age_level to be plotted (Children or Teenagers), and subject to be plotted (ELA or Math)
    Returns: A dataframe ready to be plotted with Geopandas
    '''

    # First determining the appropriate grades from age_level
    if age_level == 'Children':
        age_groups = ['2', '3', '4', '5', '6', '7', '8'] # selecting elementary/middle school grades
    elif age_level == 'Teenagers':
        age_groups = ['10','11'] # Selecting all the available high school grades ()
    else:
        age_groups = None
    
    
    # Extracting the needed information (Latitude, Longitude, and Average Standardized Test Scores) from each row in the progress_reports_19 dataset
    schools_mean_scores = data[subject][age_groups].apply(lambda x: x.mean(), axis=1)
    correct_indices = schools_mean_scores.index
    locations_correct_indices = progress_reports_19[['School_Latitude', 'School_Longitude']].loc[correct_indices]
    
    location_and_scores = pd.concat([schools_mean_scores, locations_correct_indices], axis=1).rename(columns={0:'Mean Test Score', 'School_Latitude':'Latitude', 'School_Longitude':'Longitude'})
    
    # Adding a column for the GeoPandas coordinate pair for simple plotting
    geo = [Point(xy) for xy in zip(location_and_scores.Longitude, location_and_scores.Latitude)]
    location_and_scores_geo = gpd.GeoDataFrame(location_and_scores, geometry=geo, crs='epsg:4326') # specifying the correct coordinate system
    
    # Associating each school with a neighborhood --> results in a GeoPandas dataframe with a neighborhood column for each school
    chicago_updated = chicago.to_crs('epsg:4326') # specifying the correct coordinate system for the OTHER GeoPandas dataframe
    neighborhoods_schools = gpd.sjoin(location_and_scores_geo, chicago_updated, how='inner', predicate='within')
    
    # Caclulating the Average Standardized Test Scores for each neighborhood --> results in a DF with rows corresponding to unique neighborhoods, with a column for the neighborhood's average test score
    neighborhoods_avg_test_scores = neighborhoods_schools.groupby('community')['Mean Test Score'].mean().reset_index()
    
    # Merging the average test scores with the neighborhoods dataframe --> results in a the chicago dataframe with a column for the neighborhood's average test score
    chicago_test_scores = chicago.merge(neighborhoods_avg_test_scores, on='community', how='left')

    return chicago_test_scores
